motivation: A 2026 River Test study retained silvering stage in a repeated reach-level downstream-progression model, whereas the six-project canonical overall-trajectory speed analysis showed little general Durif-stage effect. This audit tests one pre-specified finer-scale progression endpoint to distinguish aggregation-scale from true phase attenuation.

source.migration_window: rows with migration == TRUE after upstream migration classification and expert nonmigrant corrections

primary_endpoint.definition: median of finite positive row-level speed_m_s values across migration==TRUE rows for each expert-corrected activated eel
primary_endpoint.rationale: Uses consecutive-station transit-speed information and is not the classifier migration_speed variable. The median is fixed before stage inspection to reduce sensitivity to occasional extreme inter-station values without introducing an outcome-tuned upper-speed threshold.

primary_model.informative_stratum_rule: n >= 8 eligible eels and >=2 Durif stages

interpretation.ratio_gt_1_supported: More advanced silvering predicts faster active inter-station transit even though canonical overall trajectory speed shows little general stage effect.
interpretation.near_null: The weak stage signal extends from overall elapsed migration speed to a finer-scale inter-station transit endpoint.
interpretation.ratio_lt_1_supported: Advanced stage is associated with slower inter-station transit; do not reinterpret without an independently motivated mechanism.

secondary: Report project-specific primary endpoint stage coefficients only as scope diagnostics, with no subgroup rescue.
Report correlation between individual median segment speed and canonical overall speed descriptively if exact individual linkage is available.
prohibited: Do not use row-level observations as independent biological replicates.
Do not use the classifier-derived migration_speed column as the progression endpoint.
Do not tune minimum segment count, upper-speed cutoff, median/mean choice, project inclusion, or covariates after stage-result inspection.
Do not promote a significant segment-speed effect into migration success or barrier-passage causation.
